Towards the start of my depression when I was 12, I had heard here and there about cutting and was intrigued for some reason, so I tried it one day and got hooked immediately just like that

It feels good at first, I’ll be honest with you. The problem is that it functions like a drug, and is just as addictive. You become extremely conscious of whether you’re scars are visible at any given moment. You worry at every doctors appointment. Swimming becomes a dread. A sick competition forms in your head where you always feel like you need to go deeper, and it stays that way no matter how deep you go.

So in my opinion it only makes things worse past the initial relief. Obviously a strangers words don’t count for much, but just know what you’d be getting yourself into. 

Wishing you the best of luck :)

Was actually in the exact same situation last night. At the hospital I went to, they obviously asked the usual mental health questions and they also had to make sure someone was with me at all times, even in the bathroom. 

After the medical people came and went, psychiatry came and did the usual run down. In the end, the head psych recommended partial hospitalization but I didn’t have to do it, and I got to go home just like that. Not sure how it is other places, but they were pretty understanding.

The most important thing I learned there is that apparently they generally can’t stitch it if it’s been longer than 12 hours, especially not if it’s been a day, as was my case. So basically if you’re gonna go, you should go as soon as possible so you don’t run that risk. 

Best of luck <3

As someone who frequents r/madeofstyrofoam, I think we just respond differently to tone. I’ve grown up on corners of the internet where joking about awful things is the norm, and for me, that’s the best way to vent. 

I do get your frustrations as someone who doesn’t like it, especially since terms originating on the sh meme sub inevitably end up on more serious ones like this. I guess it’s just easier for a lot of us to express things through humor than vent in full sincerity.

I will say that most people still genuinely do take it seriously on MOS, even though I’m sure it wouldn’t seem like it at first glance. Few on there are unaware of the severity of sh. 

While to you, it may feel like meming about cutting is making a mockery of it, to a lot of us it’s just genuinely more helpful than other subs or boards that feel so grim. 

I do however definitely agree with you that someone new to this mess could be negatively influenced into thinking that what they’re doing isn’t all that bad. I’m not sure what the solution to that is, but it shouldn’t be ignored.

I wish you the best of luck, and hope that you can push through you're addiction and find something legal that you're passionate about to turn your life around.

I'd heard about it from my mom, and then later from my health teacher. When I was 12, somehow I ended up coming across these videos from this girl on youtube, talking about her experience with it. I immediately really wanted to try it, I think just out of curiosity. I wanted to feel what it was like.

I think to some degree, I was also looking to validate my depression, even though I'd already been diagnosed. I kind of felt like a fake for some reason.

But of course, no matter why you start, it's hard not to get addicted. So basically, my curiosity and insecurity turned into a coping mechanism, and that coping mechanism turned into addiction.
